predictions.text: A W-4 is not a fixed document. You can update it at any time by submitting a new form to your employer's HR department. If you have a life change — marriage, divorce, a child, a second job — it's worth revisiting to make sure your withholding is still accurate. The IRS withholding estimator at irs.gov is the most reliable way to check.

The annual gift tax exclusion for 2024 is $18,000 per person, per recipient. You can give up to this amount to any number of people without filing a gift tax return. Above that threshold, you need to file Form 709, but you likely won't owe tax until your lifetime total gifts exceed the federal estate tax exemption.

A Roth IRA has a contribution limit, but it does not have a limit on conversions. If you have money in a traditional IRA, you can convert any amount to a Roth in a given year — you'll owe income tax on the converted amount, but there's no cap. This is how the backdoor Roth works for high earners.

My partner and I are trying to decide whether to pay off our car loan ($9,200 left at 4.9%) or use that money to max out a Roth IRA for the year. We have 4 months of emergency fund already. What would you do?

If you switched jobs this year, your old employer's 401k is still yours and you have several options — you can leave it, roll it to your new employer's plan, or roll it to an IRA. The IRA rollover almost always gives you the most investment options and the lowest fees. The one time to skip it: if your new employer plan has institutional funds you can't access otherwise.

When calculating whether to pay off debt or invest, the comparison isn't just the interest rate vs. expected market return. Factor in: is the debt interest deductible? Is there an employer match available that represents an instant 50-100% return? Are you comparing to tax-advantaged or taxable investment returns? The simple interest rate comparison misses a lot.

When you roll over a 401k, request a direct rollover to the new institution rather than taking the check yourself. If the check is made out to you, the plan administrator is required to withhold 20% for taxes — even if you intend to roll it over. You'd then have to make up that 20% out of pocket within 60 days to avoid it being treated as a distribution.

If you have more than 20% equity in your home, you can request to have PMI removed without waiting for automatic cancellation. Contact your lender and ask about their appraisal requirements. In a market where home values have increased significantly, you may already be at 20% equity based on current value even if you're not based on original purchase price.
